summary: AWS EC2 RunInstances failed: RequestLimitExceeded during instance launch

evidence.message: Task 'Launch EC2 instance' failed: An error occurred (RequestLimitExceeded) when calling the RunInstances operation
ansible-runner-x7f33 stderr: boto3 retry exhausted after 3 attempts
amazon.aws.ec2_instance called with no retries/backoff config; inherits boto3 standard mode (3 attempts, no jitter)
Job 20 failed with the identical RequestLimitExceeded signature 3 minutes earlier on a different catalog_item (openshift-cnv-single-node)

causal_chain.statement: AWS throttled RunInstances at the account level during a burst of concurrent provisioning jobs
The instance-creation role sets no retry backoff, so boto3 defaults to 3 attempts with no jitter
Retries exhausted before the rate limit cleared, so the task failed and the job aborted
The same signature hit unrelated catalog items in the same window, confirming an account-level limit rather than a per-catalog config fault

misidentifications.theory: DNS resolution failure in the provisioning namespace
misidentifications.why_suspected: The task aborted at the connection stage, which usually correlates with DNS problems in this environment
misidentifications.why_ruled_out: Splunk shows successful DNS resolution 2s before the failure; the error was an AWS API throttle, not a lookup failure

recommendations.action: Add exponential backoff with jitter to the EC2 instance-creation role

fix.diff:
--- a/ansible/roles_ocp_workloads/aws_instance_create/tasks/main.yml
+++ b/ansible/roles_ocp_workloads/aws_instance_create/tasks/main.yml
@@ -31,6 +31,9 @@
     instance_type: "{{ aws_instance_type }}"
     image_id: "{{ aws_ami_id }}"
     wait: true
+    retries:
+      mode: adaptive
+      max_attempts: 8

recommendations.action: Cap concurrent RunInstances calls per region in the batch scheduler
recommendations.details: Spreads provisioning load so the account-level limit is not hit in bursts
